source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Description , Power on the system and enter BIOS setup.
Enable the OS Watchdog Timer feature. Save changes and exit. Allow the system to boot.

Note: This bios switch is listed under Integrated Devices.
The user must turn off OS “Automatically restart” option you: Right click My computer (W2K8) or System (Win7), Click on “advanced system settings”, Under the “Startup and Recovery” section click on “settings…”, and under the “System Failure” section there is a check box to disable “automatically Restart” by unchecking it
Input Data
The OS Watchdog Timer field is set to "Enable". POST does not display any error messages

2 Description
Run the utility attached and generate a High IRQ fault.
Input Data
The system should blue screen and reboot in 10 minutes

3 Description
During re-boot POST, see the warning message
Input Data
You should see:
Warning: a fatal error has caused system reset!'
Please check the system event log

4 Description
Enter BIOS setup and disable the OS Watchdog Timer feature. Save changes and exit. Allow the system to boot.
Input Data
The OS Watchdog Timer field is set to "disable". POST does not display any error messages.

5 Description
Run the utility attached and generate a High IRQ fault.
Input Data
The system hangs but does not reboot.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
2. The help text for the Watchdog Timer field should read:
"If your system stops responding, this watchdog timer aids in the recovery of your operating system. When this field is set to Enabled, the operating system is allowed to initialize the timer. When it is set to Disabled (the default), the timer will have no effect on the system."
3. The selections for the field should be "Enabled" and "Disabled".
4. The field should switch to "Disabled" since this is the default setting.
5. Offset 03Ch, bit 0 in the WDAT should be 1 since the Watchdog Timer is enabled in Setup.
6. This time, the table "WDAT" should not exist since the Watchdog Timer is "Disabled" in Setup.

original_test_intent: Procedure appears to validate runtime OS-watchdog recovery: with the BIOS feature enabled, a controlled High IRQ fault should remain at a blue screen until watchdog reset within ten minutes and show a fatal-reset warning; with it disabled, the same stimulus should hang without watchdog reboot. The Items name `loader Watchdog`, while the Criteria instead define BIOS field help/default and WDAT table exposure.
original_method: Change the BIOS OS Watchdog Timer, change Windows automatic-restart behavior, run an attached High IRQ fault utility in enabled and disabled phases, and observe crash, reboot, POST warning and hang. The preserved Criteria require a different BIOS/ICE/WDAT inspection flow that is fully described in physical next row 804.
manual_activity: Only after correction, an engineer changes BIOS and OS crash behavior, authorizes and launches the approved fault utility, watches console/POST, controls recovery from the disabled-state hang and restores settings. Automation may collect approved read-only ACPI, crash, boot, event and SEL evidence.
required_inputs: Engineer decision whether this row is runtime OS-watchdog recovery, BIOS UI/WDAT exposure, or separately accepted checkpoints, including what `loader Watchdog` means
Per-state matrix for BIOS value, OS automatic-restart value, watchdog timer owner/initialization, timeout and tolerance, expected crash/hang/reset/POST warning and recovery
Signed or hashed High IRQ utility, authoritative source, exact invocation, required privilege, supported OS/driver/BIOS, failure effect and cleanup
Platform-authoritative WDAT schema/table-discovery method and meaning of the source's Offset 03Ch bit 0; no guessed offset or fixed address
Dedicated non-production SUT, data backup, crash dump and event capture, serial/OOB console, boot-loop escape, BIOS/OS restore and disabled-hang recovery
safety_requirements: Do not run the unknown High IRQ utility, change watchdog/crash settings or deliberately hang the host until engineers correct the acceptance scope and approve the exact package and recovery matrix.
Do not substitute 100 AC cycles for watchdog expiration, and do not use `ipmitool -P` or any command that exposes BMC credentials.
Use only a dedicated non-production SUT with writes quiesced, verified backup/recovery, serial/OOB console and an independent timer; no unattended execution.
Export baseline BIOS, ACPI, OS, dump, event and SEL evidence before any approved clear; never erase the only crash or first-failure record.
Run one approved phase at a time and stop on wrong target, premature/late/unexpected reset, boot loop, dump failure, data/filesystem error, management loss or firmware/thermal/power anomaly.
The disabled-state expected hang requires a preapproved manual recovery action; do not automatically retry, cycle power or proceed to another phase after an anomaly.
Restore BIOS watchdog and OS automatic-restart settings, boot cleanly, validate data/filesystem and preserve dumps/logs before closure.
agent_execution_scope: Before correction, perform no DUT, BIOS, OS, fault, reboot or power action; only preserve the conflict and required engineer decision.

After approval, collect baseline/post-state BIOS exports, OS watchdog/crash settings, read-only ACPI/WDAT parses, console timestamps, crash dumps, boot/POST, event logs and SEL around engineer-controlled phases.
Report runtime reset timing, warning and disabled-state non-reset separately from BIOS UI and WDAT checkpoints; one evidence class cannot pass the other.
Do not launch fault tools, alter settings, recover hangs, expose secrets, infer unapproved WDAT offsets, clear evidence, retry or issue DUT verdicts.
engineer_actions: Correct the Review-layer purpose and acceptance matrix while preserving Master, deciding whether runtime and BIOS/WDAT are separate mandatory checkpoints.
Validate and approve the High IRQ package, exact platform/OS, BIOS and OS state transitions, timeout, console/dump capture, abort, hang recovery and rollback.
Perform or supervise destructive phases, restore the SUT and issue per-checkpoint plus overall DUT verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The AC Cycle 100 times procedure is copied from row 1525 and has no equivalent coverage for watchdog initialization, expiry, crash behavior, POST warning or WDAT. Its password command is also unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No fault or configuration command until source correction. Afterwards use only the approved utility under attended console control and an authoritative parser for state-specific WDAT evidence; keep runtime and firmware-table results separate.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All source BIOS enabled/disabled states, Windows automatic-restart instruction, High IRQ utility, ten-minute reboot statement, POST warning, disabled hang, WDAT help/default/offset clauses, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split or explicitly matrix the case into BIOS/UI and WDAT exposure checks plus runtime enabled and disabled High IRQ phases; validate the package; baseline and protect data; run each approved phase once with independent timing/console/dump capture; recover manually; restore and verify clean state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Engineer-corrected watchdog layer, BIOS/ACPI implementation, supported Windows or Project OS and validated fault driver/tool.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record system BIOS, BMC, ACPI table revision, OS/build, driver and exact fault utility hash/version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform OS Watchdog Timer, ACPI/WDAT layout and runtime fault/recovery specification; approved utility documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Does not overwrite Master; it separates the copied WDAT Criteria from runtime crash semantics and requires authoritative table parsing and destructive-fault controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only WDAT/UI evidence cannot prove expiration and reset; runtime reboot/hang evidence cannot prove the source's exact help/default/table/bit clauses. Any Project omission must be recorded.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Scope decision, state matrix, validated utility, timing, evidence, recovery and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A privileged fault injector can corrupt active I/O or produce an unrecoverable hang or reset loop before software evidence is flushed.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may use a supported modern OS, another validated equivalent fault injector or a supported WDAT parser, but must retain the original Windows/High IRQ/ICE-offset obligations, document equivalence and identify any runtime or firmware-table coverage left unverified.
expected_evidence: Preserved Master/duplicate conflict and dated engineer decision defining `loader`, runtime and BIOS/WDAT checkpoints
Approved enabled/disabled state and acceptance matrix, authoritative WDAT schema/method, BIOS/BMC/OS/driver/tool versions and utility hash
Dedicated-SUT authorization, backup/quiesce, console/OOB, independent timer, dump/event/SEL capture and hang/boot-loop recovery proof
Per-state BIOS and OS settings plus read-only ACPI/WDAT table/field evidence, without guessed offset interpretation
Enabled-phase fault start, blue-screen/hang, watchdog reset within the approved ten-minute tolerance, POST warning, clean boot, dump/event/SEL timeline
Disabled-phase same-stimulus non-reset observation for the approved interval, manual recovery, restored BIOS/OS state, data/filesystem health and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items name `loader Watchdog` and Procedure exercises OS-watchdog High IRQ crash/reboot versus hang behavior, but Criteria are the BIOS help/default and WDAT inspection clauses repeated by physical next row 804's distinct OS Watchdog procedure. Code is also reused at row 1525 for unrelated AC cycling. Runtime expiry and firmware-table exposure are separate claims and the Master does not state how they combine.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This exceeds missing Project values: AI cannot choose whether destructive runtime recovery, BIOS UI/WDAT inspection or both define completion. Executing either inferred scope could cause a crash and still fail to satisfy the preserved other scope, so DUT execution must wait for engineer correction.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its duplicate AC-cycle method and password handling as unrelated and unsafe.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and retains its state/package/recovery requirements while making the copied-next-row Criteria evidence explicit.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces PARTIAL command review with a source-semantic block and separate evidence obligations.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps the split/align resolution but adds source-next-row proof, authoritative WDAT decoding, independent timing and explicit disabled-hang recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents a deliberate host crash or 100 AC cuts from being run against a testcase whose runtime watchdog and firmware-table acceptance still disagree, while preserving every original obligation for engineer correction.
independent_technical_reasoning: WDAT/UI evidence shows firmware-described watchdog capability and configuration, whereas a High IRQ hang followed by reset shows runtime initialization, expiry and recovery. Either can succeed while the other fails. Because Criteria are copied from the adjacent static WDAT case and the Procedure deliberately crashes or hangs the host, only an engineer can define whether these are separate required checkpoints before safe execution.
